hook: My case has dragged on for years. Is there a **faster way to settle**?

slides.title: A forum to **settle**, not fight.
slides.body: A Lok Adalat helps the parties reach a compromise or settlement. It can take up cases pending in court, and disputes not yet filed in any court.

slides.title: How a pending case **gets there.**
list: One party applies, and the court sees a chance of settlement
The court finds the case suitable for a Lok Adalat

slides.title: **No court fee.** Even a refund.
slides.body: No court fee is payable when a matter is filed in a Lok Adalat. If a case referred from court is settled there, the court fee you paid is refunded.

slides.title: The award is **final.**
slides.body: A Lok Adalat award is treated as a decree of a civil court. It is final and binding on all parties, and no appeal lies to any court against it.

slides.title: No settlement? **Back to court.**
slides.body: If no compromise is reached, the record goes back to the court, which continues the case from the stage it had reached before the reference.

slides.title: Utility problem? **Permanent Lok Adalat.**
slides.body: For services like transport, post, telephone, power, water, sanitation, hospitals and insurance, you can apply before going to court (subject to a value limit). If talks fail, it can decide the dispute, unless it relates to an offence.

sources: National Legal Services Authority (nalsa.gov.in) – Lok Adalats
caption:
Stuck in a long court case? A Lok Adalat may help you settle it. 👇

1️⃣ It helps parties reach a compromise, for pending cases and disputes not yet filed in court
2️⃣ No court fee is payable, and if a case referred from court is settled, the court fee is refunded
3️⃣ The award is treated as a civil court decree. It's final and binding, with no appeal
4️⃣ No settlement? The case goes back to the court and continues from where it was
5️⃣ It can't deal with offences that are not compoundable
6️⃣ National Lok Adalats are held on a single day in courts across the country

Source: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Sec 19, 20, 21, 22A, 22C); NALSA
